answer: Reputation horizon decay. Each identity's score decays on a fixed schedule unless refreshed by verified interactions, so a clone army must be continuously maintained rather than created once. Scores also flow through a shared river of transaction history: new identities start at zero and inherit nothing. A prism rule splits rewards across independent counterparties, so self-dealing clusters earn little. Attacker cost: ongoing compute and interaction fees per clone, forever, plus zero payoff during the decay window before trust accrues.
